name: Ak-Kurum Stone Mushrooms
full: Ak-Kurum tract (valley) (Ak-Korum, Akkurum) — a slope on the right bank of the Chulyshman about 1.5 km from the mouth of the Chulcha, Chulyshman valley
near: Koo village (≈5 km); tourist bases at km 61 of the Balyktuyul–Balykcha road (left bank, opposite the tract); Balykcha village (≈15 km, at Lake Teletskoye)
elev: The pillar “mushrooms” are 1 to 7 m tall (up to 10 m per KP), the “caps” are boulders more than 2 m across; the gain from the river is ≈120 m (Turister). Absolute elevation — not found (the valley floor is ≈450–500 m)
short: A field of “stone mushrooms” — clay-and-pebble pillars up to 7 m tall with heavy boulder caps on the slope above the Chulyshman. You cross by boat and climb on foot for about an hour.
desc: Ak-Kurum is a tract (valley) on the slope of the Chulyshman’s right bank, about 15 km from Lake Teletskoye and ≈30 km below the Katu-Yaryk Pass. Dozens of “stone mushrooms” stand here — erosion pillars of clay and pebbles (former glacial deposits) topped with dense stone slabs, the “caps”. Rain and wind wash out the loose rock, while the stone on top protects the “stem” — so some mushrooms collapse and others slowly “grow”. The pillars are from 1 to 7 m tall, the caps more than 2 m. The tract has been declared a natural monument (since 1960 per Turister) and lies within the UNESCO site “Golden Mountains of Altai”. A large mushroom fell in the 1980s, and several more caps fell in the Chuya earthquake of 2003. Locals have a belief: when the last mushroom falls, the end of the world will come; and if you hold on to a “stem” and ask a question, the answer will come quickly. You can get there only from the left bank: the tourist bases at km 61 run a boat crossing, and then it is about an hour’s climb along a trail.
guide: Take the first boat at 6:30–7:00: at 7–8 in the morning the sun lights up the mushrooms, and then the slope goes into the shadow of the mountains. The climb is steep and loose, but it takes about an hour — bring water and closed shoes. Don’t go under the caps or touch the pillars: they really do fall, the last time in the 2003 earthquake. According to the belief, if you hold the “stem” of a mushroom and ask a question, the answer will come soon; test it yourself. The trail to Uchar starts from the same place.
see: The field of stone mushrooms itself and the viewpoint above it with a panorama of the Chulyshman valley; on the way — the “Shaman Rock” on the neighboring mountain (TripAdvisor); nearby — the start of the trail to Uchar, the Kurkure waterfall higher up the valley
skip: you have already seen similar pillars (Cappadocia, Crimea, the Elbrus region) and are not ready to take the road over Katu-Yaryk or a 12-hour trip from Artybash for them
diff: Easy–moderate: a boat crossing, then ≈1.5–2 km of a steep loose trail with a gain of ≈120 m, about an hour up; for the unprepared it is a “not very easy” climb
when: May–September (the season of the bases and the ferry); the crossing works from April to November (2026); in winter it is accessible if there is a boat (trips in January 2019 and 2024/25)
hours: Free access; the boat crossing — daily 6:30–21:00, April–November (2026)
daytime: Early morning (7:00–8:00) — the mushrooms are lit by the sun; in the daytime the slope is in shade most of the time
how: Drive to the tourist bases at km 61 of the Balyktuyul–Balykcha road (the left bank of the Chulyshman). By land: Aktash → Ulagan → Balyktuyul → the Katu-Yaryk Pass (≈100 km from Aktash) → ≈30 km down the valley. By water: from Artybash by ferry or motorboat to the southern shore of Lake Teletskoye, then ≈15 km along the valley. Then a boat across the Chulyshman and a climb of ≈1 h
needcar: Yes: an SUV/ferry to the valley; a boat across the river is mandatory
self: Yes: get to the tourist bases at km 61, pay for the boat and climb the trail (markings are scarce — an offline map helps)
roadtype: To the valley — the Ulagan highway and the Katu-Yaryk serpentine, or by water; along the valley — dirt road; to the mushrooms — a steep loose trail
traveltime: The crossing ≈5 min; the climb ≈1 h, the whole excursion 1.5–2 h; Artybash → mushrooms: motorboat ≈2.5 h + UAZ ≈2 h (per the tour program); the Katu-Yaryk Pass → km 61 ≈1 h (estimate)
stay: “Stone Mushrooms” campground (1.5 km below the mouth of the Chulcha, year-round, +7 913 999-68-36): a 2-person cabin 3,000 ₽, a 3-person 4,000 ₽, 4-person 5,000 ₽, a family house 7,000 ₽, an 8-person house 8,000 ₽, an ail (traditional Altai log dwelling) for 7–8 people 6,000 ₽ (2026). Nearby at km 61: “Stone Mushroom Valley” (from 4,500 ₽, 2GIS 4.8/99), “Waterfall Valley” (from 3,000 ₽, 4.9/67); the “Berezka” base at the crossing; “Golden Valley of the Chulyshman” in Koo (from 2,500 ₽)
net: Unstable: in the valley a signal appeared in 2024–2025, but with interruptions (T—Zh); KP writes that there is no signal. Operators not found
entry: No separate entry fee for the tract was found in the sources (you pay only for the boat). A border-zone permit is not needed
transfer: A boat 1,000–1,500 ₽ per boat for up to 4 people round trip (2026); transfer Ulagan – mushrooms 16,000 ₽ for up to 8 people; southern shore of Teletskoye – mushrooms 20,000 ₽ (2026)
bring: Closed shoes with a good sole (loose slope), water, a hat, cash for the boat, a camera for sunrise
warn: Do not go under the “caps” and do not climb the pillars: they collapse (1980s, the 2003 earthquake). A steep loose slope — careful on the descent. In 2026 bears are active in the valley (the nature reserve closed the neighboring trail to Uchar from 20.08). Ticks in spring and early summer. A border-zone permit is not needed
food: Meals at the “Stone Mushrooms” campground: breakfast 400 ₽, lunch 800 ₽, dinner 700 ₽, a full set 1,900 ₽ (2026); grayling from the Chulyshman
reviews: No rating for the tract itself was found on 2GIS/Yandex. The “Stone Mushrooms” campground — 4.3 (79 ratings, 2GIS); the Sputnik8 tour to the mushrooms — 4.6 (27). Pros: unusual forms, a panorama of the valley, a mystical atmosphere; cons: a long road, a steep climb, “all the bases in the valley are alike” (TripAdvisor)

p.sum: The stone mushrooms stand on the right bank of the Chulyshman, opposite the tourist bases at km 61 of the Balyktuyul–Balykcha road (≈30 km below Katu-Yaryk, ≈15 km from Lake Teletskoye). A boat across the river costs 1,000–1,500 ₽ per boat for up to 4 people round trip (2026), then ≈1 h of steep climbing (≈120 m). The best light is 7–8 in the morning. It is convenient to stay at the “Stone Mushrooms” campground (3,000–8,000 ₽ per cabin, 2026) or at the neighboring bases. From Artybash — a day tour for 12,000 ₽.
